facts.raw_span: A 5-month-old dark-skinned boy
a congenital skin lesion on the left supraclavicular area
At birth, the lesion measured 11 cm × 3.5 cm
at 5 months it measured 10 cm × 2.5 cm
a single, nonpulsatile, well-demarcated, dark brown atrophic plaque
with a linear midline depression and an elevated, compressible, soft border that was paler than the central portion
a small vein (~0.3 mm) was visible to the naked eye within the plaque
one large vein with an extensive network of small superficial branching vessels localized to the area of the atrophic plaque
Birth and neonatal history were unremarkable
the patient was healthy and not on medications
the initial differential diagnosis included smooth muscle hamartoma, semiannular lipoatrophy, and, less likely, a rapidly involuting congenital hemangioma (RICH)
a working diagnosis of probable RICH was made
